pathophysiology.summary: Acute coronary syndrome results from an acute reduction in myocardial blood flow, typically following atheromatous plaque erosion or rupture with superimposed thrombus formation.
keyMechanisms: Plaque disruption and thrombosis: partial or transient occlusion may lead to NSTEMI or unstable angina; complete coronary occlusion typically causes STEMI.
Myocardial oxygen supply-demand mismatch leads to ischaemia progressing to acute cellular necrosis.
Cardiac troponin elevation reflects myocardial injury; dynamic change helps distinguish acute injury from chronic baseline elevation in clinical context.

symptoms: Heavy, crushing, or retrosternal pressure lasting more than 15 minutes.
Radiation to the left arm, neck, jaw, back, or epigastrium.
Diaphoresis, dyspnoea, nausea, vomiting, lightheadedness, or syncope.
physicalSigns: Pallor, diaphoresis, tachycardia, bradycardia, or a new arrhythmia.
Hypotension, elevated JVP, or bibasal crackles may suggest acute heart failure or cardiogenic shock.
A normal physical examination does not exclude ACS.
redFlags: ST elevation of at least 1 mm in 2 contiguous leads, new or presumed-new LBBB, or posterior MI pattern.
Cardiogenic shock, acute pulmonary oedema, sustained VT/VF, or high-grade AV block.
Abrupt tearing pain, inter-arm blood-pressure difference over 20 mmHg, pulse deficit, or acute neurological deficit.
Unilateral absent breath sounds, hyper-resonance, tracheal deviation, or obstructive shock.
precipitants: Known coronary artery disease or previous ACS
Cardiovascular risk factors or recent exertional symptoms
Aortic disease, venous thromboembolism, or pneumothorax risk factors when clinically relevant

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Abrupt maximal-onset tearing pain, blood-pressure asymmetry, pulse deficit, neurological deficit, or new aortic regurgitation murmur. Prioritise urgent aortic imaging and haemodynamic management; avoid antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment until dissection is excluded.
Pleuritic pain, sudden dyspnoea, tachycardia, hypoxaemia, or features of DVT. Use the locally validated PE pathway for imaging and treatment decisions.

Severe respiratory distress, unilateral absent breath sounds, hyper-resonance, tracheal shift, and hypotension. Immediate decompression takes priority over diagnostic imaging when clinically suspected.
Burning epigastric pain, positional discomfort, or reproducible chest-wall tenderness. Consider only after ACS and vascular emergencies have been clinically excluded.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Perform and interpret within 10 minutes of first medical contact; repeat at 15–30 minute intervals if pain persists or recurs.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: ST elevation, ischaemic ST depression, T-wave inversion, new LBBB, or posterior MI pattern.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: A normal ECG does not exclude ACS; serial ECG assessment guides emergency reperfusion and escalation.
ruleIn.normalValue: Sinus rhythm without acute ischaemic ST-segment or T-wave change

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Draw at presentation and repeat at 1, 2, or 3 hours using the local validated assay pathway.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Dynamic rise and/or fall above the assay-specific 99th percentile.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Interpret assay-specific change with symptoms, ECG, and clinical context; a biomarker rise alone does not establish ACS.
ruleIn.normalValue: Below the assay-specific 99th percentile upper reference limit

ruleIn.modalityTarget: FBC, U&Es, LFTs, glucose, coagulation profile, and lipid panel.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Renal function, bleeding risk, metabolic abnormality, and contrast suitability
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Findings that modify antithrombotic selection, dosing, and acute risk assessment.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Establish baseline renal function and bleeding risk before antithrombotic treatment or contrast exposure.
ruleIn.normalValue: Use local adult laboratory reference intervals; no clinically important renal impairment, anaemia, coagulopathy, or electrolyte disturbance

ruleOut.targetCondition: Pulmonary oedema, pneumothorax, widened mediastinum, or consolidation
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Features supporting an alternative thoracic cause or complication.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: A chest radiograph may support an alternative diagnosis but does not exclude ACS or reliably exclude aortic dissection.
ruleOut.normalValue: No acute pulmonary oedema, pneumothorax, focal consolidation, or widened mediastinal contour

ruleOut.testName: CT pulmonary angiogram or CT aortogram
ruleOut.modalityTarget: High clinical suspicion for PE or aortic dissection.
ruleOut.targetCondition: Pulmonary arterial occlusion or aortic intimal flap
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Imaging evidence of PE or aortic dissection.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use targeted imaging when the clinical suspicion is high; do not delay time-critical primary PCI for diagnostic imaging in STEMI.
ruleOut.normalValue: No pulmonary arterial filling defect or aortic intimal flap

clinicalManagement.title: Immediate emergency assessment
actions: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, observations, and pain score; maintain continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry.
Obtain a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes, establish IV access, and draw hs-troponin and baseline laboratory tests.
Give oxygen only for saturation below 90% or severe respiratory distress.
Before antithrombotic treatment, assess for aortic dissection, tension pneumothorax, PE, and other life-threatening alternatives.

branches.condition: Persistent severe pain after initial assessment
actions: Use GTN and opioid analgesia only after contraindication and haemodynamic review under the local emergency protocol.

clinicalManagement.title: STEMI reperfusion pathway
actions: Activate the catheterisation laboratory for primary PCI when the local first-medical-contact to device target can be met.
When timely PCI is not available, consider fibrinolysis only after confirming eligibility and absence of absolute contraindications, followed by immediate transfer to a PCI-capable centre.
Select antiplatelet and anticoagulant treatment through the current Saudi/local ACS pathway, with renal function, bleeding risk, and reperfusion strategy documented.

clinicalManagement.title: NSTE-ACS risk stratification and strategy
actions: Use serial ECGs, hs-troponin trends, and validated HEART and GRACE risk assessment.
Escalate immediately for refractory angina, haemodynamic instability, cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, or sustained VT/VF.
Consider early invasive assessment for confirmed NSTEMI, dynamic ST-T changes, or high-risk GRACE score, following the local pathway.
Choose DAPT and anticoagulation only after individual bleeding risk, renal function, and planned invasive strategy are reviewed.

clinicalManagement.title: Low-risk rule-out and safety net
actions: Consider discharge only after a negative validated rapid hs-troponin pathway, HEART score of 3 or lower, non-dynamic ECGs, and clinical exclusion of non-coronary emergencies.
Arrange rapid-access chest-pain clinic or outpatient cardiology follow-up within the locally approved timeframe.
Give clear emergency return precautions for recurrent or worsening symptoms.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: ST elevation of at least 1 mm in 2 contiguous leads or another diagnostic ECG pattern requiring immediate specialist interpretation.
hs-cTn above the assay-specific 99th percentile with a dynamic rise and/or fall, interpreted with symptoms and ECG.
Negative validated serial hs-cTn pathway, HEART score 3 or lower, non-dynamic ECGs, and no alternative life-threatening diagnosis.

teaching.scope: Educational draft for adult acute chest-pain triage. Follow current Saudi/local emergency, cardiology, and formulary pathways for patient care.
learningObjectives: Recognise ACS red flags and life-threatening non-coronary alternatives.
Use serial ECG and hs-troponin assessment in a validated local pathway.
Escalate immediately for STEMI, shock, pulmonary oedema, malignant arrhythmia, or suspected aortic dissection.
pitfalls: Do not delay indicated reperfusion for non-essential imaging.
Do not use this draft as a prescribing protocol or substitute for local pathway confirmation.
Do not attribute atypical or persistent symptoms to a benign diagnosis before dangerous causes are considered.
keyPoints: A normal initial ECG does not exclude ACS.
Troponin must be interpreted as a dynamic biomarker in the clinical context.
Exclude aortic dissection before antithrombotic treatment when the presentation is suggestive.

references.title: NICE CG95: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin

patientEducation: Call emergency services immediately if chest pain recurs, radiates to the arm or jaw, or is accompanied by diaphoresis or dyspnoea.
Explain the follow-up plan, medicines, and warning signs using teach-back where possible.
lifestyleAndDiet: Provide smoking-cessation support, dietary advice, and activity guidance after stabilisation.
Offer formal cardiac rehabilitation after confirmed ACS when appropriate.
mdtReferrals: Pharmacy and primary care for medicine reconciliation and cardiovascular risk reduction
dischargeCriteria: Validated ACS diagnostic pathway completed with serial hs-troponin assessment and non-ischaemic or non-dynamic ECGs when discharge is appropriate.
Chest pain resolved and vital signs stable.
Clear follow-up plan, secondary-prevention plan where indicated, and emergency return precautions documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: For low-risk discharge, arrange rapid-access chest-pain clinic or outpatient cardiology follow-up within the locally approved timeframe. For confirmed ACS, arrange cardiology follow-up and cardiac rehabilitation.
